name: Flemish Béguinages
description: The Flemish Béguinages are thirteen walled villages-within-towns across Flanders, founded from the 13th century for béguines, devout women who lived in community without taking vows or leaving the world. Behind their gates, rows of whitewashed or brick houses cluster around a church and quiet green courtyards, with practical buildings such as bakeries and breweries once serving residents. They remain peaceful, picturesque pockets of medieval life.
